sentiment.rationale: The document reports a significant GAAP loss per share of ($7.14) and a core loss per share of ($7.47), primarily driven by a $4.9 billion charge on the 777X program due to a schedule delay to 2027. While revenue improved and free cash flow turned positive, the forward guidance for 2025 free cash flow is approximately ($2.5B), indicating continued cash burn. The structural risk of the 777X certification delay and the ongoing production stabilization efforts, despite some positive operational milestones, lead to a bearish forward outlook.

summary.revenue: $23.3 billion, up 30% from $17.8 billion in 3Q24, primarily reflecting 160 commercial deliveries.
summary.eps: GAAP diluted loss per share of ($7.14), compared to ($9.97) in 3Q24. Core loss per share (non-GAAP) of ($7.47), compared to ($10.44) in 3Q24.
summary.guidance: 2025 estimate: Operating cash flow ~$0.5B, free cash flow (non-GAAP) ~($2.5B). 737 production to increase to 42 per month (jointly agreed with FAA in October). 777X first delivery now anticipated in 2027.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin of (20.5)%, improved from (32.3)% in 3Q24. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) of (21.7)%, improved from (33.6)% in 3Q24.
key_risks: 777X program charge of $4.9 billion due to updated certification timeline and first delivery now anticipated in 2027.
Ongoing production stabilization efforts for 737 and 787 programs.
Pending acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems, including satisfaction of closing conditions and realizing anticipated benefits.
Reliance on fixed-price contracts and U.S. government contracts.
Potential adverse developments in new or pending litigation and/or government inquiries or investigations.
Work stoppages or other labor disruptions.
Dependence on subcontractors and suppliers, as well as availability of highly skilled labor and raw materials.
key_opportunities: Backlog of $636 billion, including over 5,900 commercial airplanes valued at $535 billion.
Defense, Space & Security secured a contract from U.S. Space Force to enhance strategic satellite communication capabilities.
Global Services captured an award from U.S. Navy for F/A-18 aircraft landing gear repair and announced a strategic agreement with Korean Air for predictive maintenance analytics.
737 production rate increase to 42 per month agreed with FAA.
787 program progressing on investments to expand South Carolina operations.
